response.sql: WITH tif_counts AS (SELECT o.timespan AS timespan, COUNT(*) AS rm_count FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = r.ordervault WHERE o.timespan IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.timespan), shares AS (SELECT timespan, rm_count, rm_count * 1.0 / SUM(rm_count) OVER () AS share FROM tif_counts) SELECT timespan, rm_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS share_diff_from_avg FROM shares ORDER BY timespan

assumptions.assumption: The inner join on riskandmargin.ordervault = orders.recordvault drops risk/margin records with no matching order, as the request specifies. Each risk/margin record is counted once, so an order with several records contributes several counts.

Orders with a NULL timespan are excluded because NULL is not a time-in-force value. The average share is the unweighted mean of the per-value shares, and the difference is signed (share minus average) rather than absolute.

alternatives.interpretation: The difference from the average share is an absolute magnitude rather than a signed difference, so the sign of the deviation is discarded.
alternatives.sql: WITH tif_counts AS (SELECT o.timespan AS timespan, COUNT(*) AS rm_count FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = r.ordervault WHERE o.timespan IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.timespan), shares AS (SELECT timespan, rm_count, rm_count * 1.0 / SUM(rm_count) OVER () AS share FROM tif_counts) SELECT timespan, rm_count, share, ABS(share - AVG(share) OVER ()) AS abs_share_diff_from_avg FROM shares ORDER BY timespan

alternatives.interpretation: Orders with a NULL timespan are kept as their own time-in-force group, so they receive a count, share, and deviation like any other value.
